BiblicalUsage: Jethro is Moses' father-in-law, the priest of Midian who shelters the fugitive and advises the lawgiver. In Exodus 3:1 Moses keeps the flock of "Jethro his father in law, the priest of Midian," and it is there that the burning bush appears. In Exodus 4:18 Moses asks Jethro's leave to return to Egypt, and in Exodus 18:1 Jethro hears "all that God had done for Moses" and brings Zipporah and the sons to him in the wilderness.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jethro is the quiet man behind the great man. I hold that the priest of Midian who gave Moses shelter, a wife, and later wise counsel in Exodus 18 shows me that God works through family and friendship as much as through miracles, and that listening to good advice is itself an act of faith.
